# `cfmat.portfolio`

<!-- generated by tools/gen_api_docs.py; do not edit -->

Risk measurement and portfolio construction (M13, M14).

```text
The package namespace re-exports the construction methods
(``from cfmat import portfolio; portfolio.hrp_weights(...)``).

    risk          VaR, expected shortfall, VaR backtests, position sizing, Kelly, stress tests
    construction  min-variance, max-Sharpe, risk parity, HRP, rolling strategy allocation
```

### `cfmat.portfolio.construction`

Portfolio construction (M14): mean–variance, risk parity and Hierarchical Risk Parity. Inputs are annualised ``mu`` (expected returns) and ``cov`` (covariance) as numpy arrays or pandas objects.

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `allocation_returns` | `def allocation_returns(returns: pd.DataFrame, weights: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Combined return when weights decided at close t are held over t+1. |
| `efficient_frontier` | `def efficient_frontier(mu, cov, n_points: int = 30, long_only: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame` | Minimum-variance portfolios for a range of target returns. |
| `hrp_weights` | `def hrp_weights(returns: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Hierarchical Risk Parity (López de Prado, 2016). |
| `max_sharpe_weights` | `def max_sharpe_weights(mu, cov, rf: float = 0.0, long_only: bool = True) -> pd.Series` | Maximum-Sharpe (tangency) weights; unstable because expected returns are noisy. |
| `min_variance_weights` | `def min_variance_weights(cov, long_only: bool = True) -> pd.Series` | Minimum-variance weights (long-only by default, fully invested). |
| `portfolio_stats` | `def portfolio_stats(weights, mu, cov, rf: float = 0.0) -> dict[str, float]` | Expected return, volatility and Sharpe ratio of ``weights``. |
| `risk_contributions` | `def risk_contributions(weights, cov) -> np.ndarray` | Share of total variance contributed by each asset (sums to 1). |
| `risk_parity_weights` | `def risk_parity_weights(cov) -> pd.Series` | Equal risk contribution via the convex log-barrier formulation. |
| `rolling_allocation` | `def rolling_allocation(returns: pd.DataFrame, method: str = 'inverse_vol', lookback: int = 126, rebalance: int = 21) -> pd.DataFrame` | Weights across strategy sleeves, re-estimated every ``rebalance`` bars from the trailing ``lookback`` bars only (weights decided at each rebalance close). |

### `cfmat.portfolio.risk`

Risk measurement and position sizing (M13).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `atr_stop_qty` | `def atr_stop_qty(capital: float, risk_fraction: float, atr_value: float, atr_multiple: float = 2.0, lot_size: int = 1) -> int` | Volatility-based sizing: stop placed ``atr_multiple`` ATRs away. |
| `expected_shortfall` | `def expected_shortfall(returns: pd.Series, alpha: float = 0.975) -> float` | Average loss on the days worse than VaR (a.k.a. CVaR). |
| `fixed_fractional_qty` | `def fixed_fractional_qty(capital: float, risk_fraction: float, entry: float, stop: float, lot_size: int = 1) -> int` | Shares (rounded down to whole lots) so that hitting ``stop`` loses ``risk_fraction`` of ``capital``. |
| `historical_var` | `def historical_var(returns: pd.Series, alpha: float = 0.99) -> float` | Historical VaR at ``alpha`` as a positive loss fraction. |
| `kelly_fraction` | `def kelly_fraction(returns: pd.Series) -> float` | Continuous-time Kelly leverage mu / sigma² (per-period moments). |
| `kupiec_test` | `def kupiec_test(breaches: pd.Series, alpha: float = 0.99) -> dict[str, float]` | Kupiec proportion-of-failures test of a VaR model. |
| `monte_carlo_var` | `def monte_carlo_var(returns: pd.Series, alpha: float = 0.99, n_sims: int = 100000, seed: int \| None = None) -> float` | Bootstrap VaR: resample historical returns with replacement. |
| `parametric_var` | `def parametric_var(returns: pd.Series, alpha: float = 0.99) -> float` | Gaussian (variance–covariance) VaR. Understates risk when tails are fat. |
| `portfolio_var` | `def portfolio_var(weights: np.ndarray, cov: np.ndarray, alpha: float = 0.99, value: float = 1.0) -> float` | Parametric VaR of a portfolio from a covariance matrix of returns. |
| `scale_var` | `def scale_var(one_day_var: float, horizon_days: int) -> float` | Square-root-of-time rule (assumes i.i.d. returns). |
| `stress_test` | `def stress_test(positions: dict[str, float], shocks: dict[str, dict[str, float]]) -> pd.DataFrame` | Rupee P&L of ``positions`` (symbol → exposure) under named scenarios (scenario → {symbol: return}). |
| `volatility_target_leverage` | `def volatility_target_leverage(returns: pd.Series, target_vol: float = 0.1, lookback: int = 20, max_leverage: float = 2.0, periods: int = 252) -> pd.Series` | Leverage that scales exposure to hit ``target_vol``, using only past data. |
